dedupe_keys.name: satellietdataportaal netherlands space agency satellite data portal

description: The Satellietdataportaal of the Netherlands Space Agency gives free access for users in the Netherlands to raw and pre-processed satellite data of the country, with a focus on high-resolution imagery. It offers optical data, images in visible and infrared light, and radar data, which work at night and through cloud and suit the tracking of floods and ground movement, as both archive and recent acquisitions. Data was first bought for the European Netherlands, and since 2021 some high-resolution acquisitions cover Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, without radar. All data can be viewed in an online viewer, and the manuals describe an API. The licence page explains that the imagery is commercial data owned by suppliers (Pléiades Neo, SuperView, TripleSat, PlanetScope and RapidEye, Radarsat-2, Hyperscout-2, SPOT-6/7, Formosat-2, DMC) for which the Dutch government bought usage rights for Dutch users, so it is not open data, and each dataset has its own end user licence; Sentinel-2 follows the Copernicus legal notice. Caveats: use is limited to eligible Dutch users under the supplier licences, and the site is in Dutch. Coverage is the Netherlands. It supports asset mapping, land and water monitoring, and flood and ground movement analysis for infrastructure; the related record is the DLR EOC Geoservice.
